_meta.what: Debris chunk meshes for the VehicleDamage / StructureDamage particle systems of the N64 Command & Conquer, decoded from cnc_eu.z64.
_meta.triangle_record: matches the pack: (int32 tex, u8 mode, u8 wrap, 3 x {f32 x,y,z,u,v; u8 r,g,b,a}); tex -1 = untextured; mode 0 opaque / 1 cutout; wrap = cmS | cmT<<2 (bit0 mirror, bit1 clamp)
_meta.units: vertex positions are MESH units; 1024 mesh units x the console's 0.25 chunk scale = 256 leptons = one cell, so the renderer's MODEL_SCALE (1/1024) is exactly the birth scale

draw.dispatch: RAM 0x8005002C reads sys+0x10: 0 -> tri sprite 0x80050060, 1 -> quad sprite 0x80050298, 2|3 -> mesh 0x80050558, >=4 -> nothing
draw.per_particle_dl: particle+0x3C; when it is NULL and sys+0x10 == 2 the system's own sys+0x14 is used instead (no system in this game does that)
draw.house_byte: particle+0x3A, read as SIGNED at RAM 0x80050618; -1 skips the TLUT selector entirely, anything else calls RAM 0x80055D08
draw.matrix: build_matrix RAM 0x8005EFE8: row-major, rows 0..2 = scale * transpose(Rz(ez) Ry(ey) Rx(ex)), row 3 = world position, emitted as G_MTX 0xDA380003 = MODELVIEW | LOAD | NOPUSH
draw.scale: the particle's own size field (particle+0x28) is the uniform scale; the draw skips the particle when it is exactly 0.0 (RAM 0x8004FFF0)
draw.entry_rendermode: 0x00552078 (G_RM_AA_ZB_OPA_SURF2), emitted by RAM 0x80055EC4 with flag bit 0 at RAM 0x80056E48, immediately before the two mesh systems draw
draw.pass_order: the 8 sprite systems draw first (RAM 0x80056C9C..0x80056E24), then the state restore, then VehicleDamage (sys+0x68) and StructureDamage (sys+0x9C) LAST
draw.sprite_rendermode: 0x005049D8 (G_RM_AA_ZB_XLU_SURF2, no depth write) is set only for sys+0x10 < 2; the guard at RAM 0x8004F904 skips it for the mesh systems

tumble.formula: deg_i = particle[+0x30] * 0.05 * (byte_i - 127.0), with byte_0 = (node>>8)&0xFF, byte_1 = (node>>4)&0xFF, byte_2 = node&0xFF of the particle NODE's own RAM address; deg_0/1/2 are passed to build_matrix as the X, Y and Z euler angles
tumble.life_field: particle+0x30 is life REMAINING and counts DOWN (RAM 0x8004EFB4), so the chunk spins fastest at birth and unwinds to zero at death
tumble.determinism: the node address is an allocator artefact, NOT a random draw. A deterministic renderer must substitute a per-particle seed drawn from the sim RNG; see the report.

shrink.formula: if size != 0.0: size += sizeGrow;  then life -= 1
shrink.note: 0.25 / 0.005 = exactly 50 ticks, and the sources' life is 40..50 ticks, so a chunk shrinks linearly to nothing over its whole life. There is no clamp: a chunk that outlived 50 ticks would invert.
shrink.velocity: pos += vel then vel += accel each tick (RAM 0x8004EF6C/0x8004EF80); accel = the visual record's +0x1C..+0x24 = (0, -2, 0)

selection.formula: particle[+0x3C] = sys[+0x14][ rand() % sys[+0x18] ]  with sys[+0x18] = 7
selection.rand: RAM 0x8005A0E0, LCG seed = seed*0x41C64E6D + 0x3039, returns ((seed*A + 0x303A) >> 16) & 0x7FFF, so the modulo is non-negative
selection.call_site: RAM 0x8004F278, inside the action integrator's mesh branch (taken only when sys+0x10 == 3, tested at RAM 0x8004F1CC)
selection.meaning: each chunk particle picks one of its system's 7 display lists UNIFORMLY AT RANDOM at spawn; the choice never changes afterwards
selection.house: the house byte written into particle+0x3A is the VISUAL sub-record's +0x3A, taken from the action's visual pointer (action+0x8, set at RAM 0x8004EA70). For debris that record is 0x800A202C: variant 0 has house 0 (GDI table ROM 0x98F30), variant 1 has house 1 (Nod/neutral table ROM 0x99130)
selection.alpha: the chunk allocator hardcodes alpha slope 1 and cap 255 (RAM 0x8004E8FC / 0x8004E904); the mesh draw never reads the alpha, so it is dead for chunks
selection.colour: the mesh branch SKIPS the set-colour call at RAM 0x8004F344, so a chunk particle keeps the allocator's white and the visual record's colour bytes are dead for chunks too

house_tluts.note: no chunk display list issues G_LOADTLUT; every one of them sets G_SETOTHERMODE_H TEXTLUT = 0x8000 (G_TT_RGBA16) and samples whatever the selector last loaded
